sourceEvidence.label: ServerManager authentication, authorization, audit, and node-token source

assessment.summary: A capability-scoped control-plane credential can support automation without distributing the node-wide worker token.

nonNegotiables: Keep node bearer tokens internal to the control plane.
Apply user permission and key capability changes on the next request.
assumptions: External agents are operator controlled and can protect an Authorization bearer secret.
No measured latency, memory, or concurrent key-volume target was supplied.
The native single-control-plane deployment remains the target.

opportunities.title: Make external automation a bounded, attributable principal
opportunities.summary: Authenticate automation at the control plane with server-bound, scope-bound, expiring keys whose authority is intersected with live user RBAC.
opportunities.diagnosis: Without a machine principal, automation must reuse a browser credential or bypass the control plane with the node-wide worker token.

evidence.claim: Automation API keys are deferred and node tokens are the current API-to-worker credential.
The reserved api_keys table lacks server scopes, action scopes, revocation, and usage metadata.
Authenticated API traffic accepts JWT bearer tokens and narrow single-use query tickets.
Server authorization is live but global administrators bypass server permission checks.
Server routes already map dangerous actions to granular permissions.
Audit rows attribute actions to users but not machine credentials.
The API decrypts the full-authority node token for worker calls.
The worker authorizes one shared bearer token without per-user, per-server, or per-action restrictions.
The control plane is the least-drifting owner for a first machine-authorization capability because it already owns resource identity, permissions, and audit.

desiredInvariants: Node tokens never leave the control plane.
Every machine request satisfies key validity, route boundary, server allowlist, key scope, and current user RBAC.
Global-admin ownership never bypasses key restrictions.
Raw key material is shown once, stored only as a hash, and never accepted in a query string.
Every machine mutation is attributable to both the user and key.

options.title: Distribute the shared node token
options.summary: Let automation call the worker directly with its existing full-authority secret.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The shared token remains overprivileged and bypasses control-plane policy.

tradeoffs.assessment: Possession grants the worker's node-wide surface without user RBAC or per-key attribution.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Enumerate worker routes reachable with the node token.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new hop or lookup is introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No benchmark needed unless a client proxy is added.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new retained state is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm no client-side proxy is introduced.

tradeoffs.assessment: Compromise recovery rotates the same credential used by the API and worker.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise node-token rotation and record control-plane interruption.

tradeoffs.assessment: Callers are indistinguishable and revocation is coarse.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review audit/log actor data from direct worker calls.

tradeoffs.assessment: It can be used immediately but creates future secret-rotation debt.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Document every place the token must be installed and rotated.

residualRisks: Full node compromise from one leaked automation credential.

migrationNotes: Rotate any node token already shared.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop distribution and rotate the node token.

options.title: Add scoped control-plane access keys
options.summary: Use expiring, revocable server capabilities intersected with the owner's live authorization.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Adds the missing machine principal, capability bounds, lifecycle, and audit attribution.
Keeps the shared worker token internal; worker TLS and exposure controls still apply.

tradeoffs.assessment: Machine authority is server-bound, scope-bound, expiring, revocable, and dynamically intersected with user RBAC.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the authorization matrix including an admin-owned narrow key.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each request adds one indexed key lookup and capability checks but no network hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark JWT and key-authenticated status polling.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-request data is bounded by one key's scope and server arrays.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure allocations with representative maximum key metadata.

tradeoffs.assessment: A compromised key can be revoked independently; authentication still depends on the existing SQLite control plane.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Race requests with rotation and revocation and verify immediate failure.

tradeoffs.assessment: Named keys, last use, rotation, and audit attribution support incident response.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Perform a create-use-rotate-revoke drill through the public TLS endpoint.

tradeoffs.assessment: The schema and auth path are additive and existing JWT/worker protocols stay compatible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run fresh and upgrade migration tests plus all existing API tests.

residualRisks: A legitimately broad console or file-write scope remains dangerous inside its allowlist.
Client-side secret theft is not prevented.
The API remains the authorization trusted computing base.

acceptanceCriteria: Raw keys are one-time and hashed at rest.
Key and live user restrictions both apply.
Machine actions identify user and key.
migrationNotes: Roll out first with a read-only short-lived key.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revoke all keys and disable machine authentication; retain additive columns until maintenance.

options.title: Introduce an automation or MCP gateway
options.summary: Put model-facing tools, approvals, and short-lived delegation in a separate service.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Adds isolation but still needs a safe delegated API credential and synchronized policy.

tradeoffs.assessment: A separate trust domain can mediate tools and approvals, but becomes a new security-critical component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model the concrete gateway transport, credential issuer, and approval flow.

tradeoffs.assessment: Every action adds a network hop, serialization, and a second policy evaluation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark end-to-end tool calls against explicit latency SLOs.

tradeoffs.assessment: A new process retains connections, policy, and request state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure gateway RSS and per-session growth under expected concurrency.

tradeoffs.assessment: The gateway adds a failure domain, retries, and backpressure requirements despite better compromise containment.
Deployment, monitoring, secret rotation, and cross-service audit correlation all expand.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype the on-call runbook and correlation flow.

tradeoffs.assessment: A new protocol and policy layer must be introduced while the current API remains available.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define compatibility and staged cutover tests for a concrete client.

residualRisks: Policy drift between gateway tools and API routes.

workPackages: Defer until untrusted tenants, approval workflows, or MCP transport are concrete requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: A future design has explicit tenant, approval, and delegation requirements.
migrationNotes: Use scoped API keys as the rollback and bootstrap path.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the gateway and use scoped control-plane keys.

opportunities.recommendation: Use scoped control-plane access keys now; choose an isolated gateway when untrusted tenants, approvals, or a standardized tool transport justify its additional boundary.

openQuestions: Whether production should cap key lifetime below 90 days.
Whether files.read belongs in the default diagnosis preset.
Whether a future MCP transport should be client-side or an isolated gateway.
